title: WASABI: Wasserstein Sampling via Bridge Interpolants
abstract: arXiv:2610.41958v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Sampling from Boltzmann distributions is a fundamental problem in physics, chemistry, and biology. We introduce WAsserstein SAmpling via Bridge Interpolants (WASABI), a method that trains a diffusion model to generate samples from a target Boltzmann distribution given access only to the energy function. WASABI minimizes the KL divergence between the distribution generated by its diffusion model and the Boltzmann target using Wasserstein gradient flows. This approach builds on a principle underlying classical sampling methods such as Langevin dynamics. However, applying Wasserstein gradient flows to diffusion models is challenging because the updates require the gradient of the model's own log density, which is generally intractable. We derive a practical training algorithm that avoids computing this gradient. Once trained, WASABI can generate new samples without further evaluations of the energy or its gradient. tldr: 提出WASABI方法，利用Wasserstein梯度流和桥插值训练扩散模型，仅凭能量函数即可从玻尔兹曼分布中采样，且避免了难以计算的对数密度梯度，训练完成后无需再评估能量或其梯度。
en_tdlr: WASABI trains a diffusion model to sample from Boltzmann distributions using only the energy function, leveraging Wasserstein gradient flows with a practical algorithm that avoids the intractable log-density gradient, enabling sample generation without further energy evaluations once trained.
